name: function-gallery
title: Expression function gallery
summary: Eight labelled mini-plots, one per expression function (sin, cos, clamp, lerp, step, fract, abs, pow), each a pathExpression over a[0] in −1..1, on cards laid out by a loop.
prompt: Draw a cheat-sheet grid of small plots of sin, cos, clamp, lerp, step, fract, abs and pow, each labelled.
teaches: Call the expression functions with the argument orders RemoteCompose uses: clamp(min, max, x), lerp(a, b, t), step(x, edge), pow(x, n)
Plot each function as a pathExpression in a[0] (start -1, end 1), with y = baseline − height·f
Lay out repeated cards from a loop index with i % 4 and floor(i / 4)

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: clamp takes (min, max, value): clamp(x, -0.5, 0.5) clamps to the empty range and returns a constant
step(x, edge) is 1 when x > edge, so step(0, x) is the mirror image of the usual GLSL step(edge, x)
fract(x) is x − trunc(x), negative for negative x; shift the argument positive for a 0..1 sawtooth
flags 4 (LINEAR) joins the samples with straight segments; without it the path is splined and the step corners round off. A sharp jump also needs enough samples (count 201 here)

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: 68 - 56 * clamp(-0.5, 0.5, a[0] * 1.5): a ramp with flat ends
eight cards from one loop: left 6 + (i % 4) * 88, top 8 + floor(i / 4) * 106

check.describe: sin and cos one period each, clamp a ramp with flat ends, lerp a straight line, step a jump at the centre, fract four teeth, abs a V, pow a cubic rise. Resized, the background fills the box and the drawing scales uniformly to fit, centred.
